extracted.intended_audience: ORR-funded care provider facilities, PRS (post-release services) providers, contractors, and ORR staff responsible for care of unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_short: ORR care standards for unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards governing care, recordkeeping, monitoring, staffing, behavior management, language access, healthcare, and post-release services for unaccompanied children in ORR custody and for PRS providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS continuation period
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS for the unaccompanied child shall presumptively continue for not less than six months or until the unaccompanied child turns 18, whichever occurs first; or until the PRS provider assesses the unaccompanied child and determines PRS are no longer needed, but in that case for not less than six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS provider case file maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall maintain comprehensive, accurate, and current case files on unaccompanied children that are kept confidential and secure at all times and shall be accessible to ORR upon request. PRS providers shall keep all case file information together in the PRS provider's physical and electronic files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS providers shall upload all PRS documentation on services provided to unaccompanied children and sponsors to ORR's case management system within seven (7) days of completion of the services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management and retention policies
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall have written policies and procedures for organizing and maintaining the content of active and closed case files, which incorporate ORR policies and procedures and address preventing physical damage or destruction of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before providing PRS, providers shall establish administrative and physical controls to prevent unauthorized access to both electronic and physical records; may not release records to third parties without ORR approval; if no longer providing PRS must provide all active and closed case file records to ORR per ORR instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall have written policy and procedure in place that protects the sensitive information of released unaccompanied children from access by unauthorized users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS providers shall explain to released children and sponsors how, when, and under what circumstances sensitive information may be shared; providers shall have appropriate controls on information-sharing within their network, including subcontractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PRS provider is concerned about the unaccompanied child's safety and well-being, the PRS provider shall document a Notification of Concern (NOC) and report the concern(s) to ORR and, as applicable, appropriate investigative agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS providers shall document and submit NOCs to ORR within 24 hours of first suspicion or knowledge of the event(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case closure procedures for PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall formally close a case when ORR terminates PRS in accordance with the regulation and shall follow ORR instructions and relevant forms when closing a case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensure or ORR alternative for standard programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs shall be licensed by an appropriate State or Federal agency, or meet other requirements specified by ORR if licensure is unavailable to programs providing services to unaccompanied children in their State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with state/local codes and resolution of conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must comply with applicable State child welfare laws and State and local building, fire, health, and safety codes, or other requirements specified by ORR if licensure is unavailable; ORR will review conflicts between ORR regulations and State law to ensure statutory responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State law or license conflicts with an ORR employee's duties within the scope of ORR employment, the ORR employee must abide by their Federal duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of proper physical care and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide suitable living accommodations, food adequate in variety, quality, and quantity per USDA Dietary Guidelines, always-available drinking water, appropriate clothing, grooming/hygiene items, access to toilets and sinks, adequate temperature control and ventilation, and adequate supervision to protect children from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized needs assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each child must receive an individualized needs assessment including initial intake forms; identification and history; identification of special needs requiring intervention; an educational assessment and plan; whether an indigenous language speaker; assessment of family relationships and interactions; statement of religious preference; assessment of personal goals, strengths and weaknesses; and identifying information regarding immediate family, relatives, or others who may assist in reunification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment elements are enumerated (biographic, family, migration, health, substance use, mental health, etc.) and must identify immediate intervention needs (e.g., trafficking indicators trigger notification to ACF Office of Trafficking in Persons within 24 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational services requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide educational services appropriate to the child's development, communication skills, and disability in a structured classroom setting Monday through Friday, concentrating primarily on basic academic competencies and secondarily on English Language Training (ELT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes instruction and materials in needed languages; basic academic instruction in science, social studies, math, reading, writing, physical education; provide reading materials in languages other than English for leisure time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreation and leisure time plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities must include daily outdoor activity, weather permitting, at least one hour per day of large muscle activity and one hour per day of structured leisure time activities (not television); increase to at least three hours on days when school is not in session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual counseling frequency and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one individual counseling session per week conducted by certified counseling staff to review progress, establish objectives, and address developmental and crisis-related needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group counseling frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Group counseling sessions at least twice a week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acculturation and adaptation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information and services that develop social and interpersonal skills needed to live independently and responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions must meet immediate needs for food, hydration, hygiene, and provide clean clothing and bedding; include initial intake assessments covering biographic, family, migration, health, substance use, and mental health history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If answers indicate possible human trafficking or labor exploitation, the care provider must notify the ACF Office of Trafficking in Persons within 24 hours; provide comprehensive orientation (program purpose, rules, rights, legal assistance availability, immigration/employment info, Ombuds info) in simple non-technical terms and in a language the child understands; assist contacting family following ORR Guide and safety procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and cultural accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, provide access to religious services of the child's choice, celebrate culture-specific events/holidays, be culturally aware in daily activities and menus, and cover various cultures in educational services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitation and confidential contact with family
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured visitation and contact with family regardless of immigration status designed to encourage visitation; provide at least 15 minutes of phone or video contact three times a week with parents/legal guardians/family/caregivers in a private space ensuring confidentiality at no cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff shall respect the child's privacy while reasonably preventing unauthorized release of the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance with family unification and guardianship
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide assistance designed to identify and verify relatives in the U.S. and abroad and assistance in obtaining legal guardianship when necessary for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal services information provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information regarding availability of free legal assistance, right to counsel at no expense to government, right to a removal hearing before an immigration judge, ability to apply for asylum with USCIS, and ability to request voluntary departure in lieu of removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and education on child labor laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information about U.S. child labor laws and education around permissible work opportunities in a manner sensitive to age, culture, and native language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age/culture/language-sensitive service delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver services in a manner sensitive to the age, culture, native language, and complex needs of each unaccompanied child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized service plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a comprehensive, realistic individual service plan based on the needs identified by the individualized needs assessment; implement and coordinate through case management; identify person-centered goals with measurable outcomes and steps to achieve them; develop with child input and review/update regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children ages 14+ should be given a copy of the plan; younger children should be given a copy when appropriate; plans shall be in the child's native language or other auxiliary aid and use concise, concrete sentences and/or visual aids and check for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR monitoring activities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR monitors facilities for compliance using desk monitoring, routine day-long site visits, site visits in response to reports or specific investigations, and monitoring visits as part of comprehensive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action process
rubrics_metrics.description: If ORR finds a facility out of compliance, ORR will communicate concerns in writing with a monitoring/site visit report listing corrective actions and best-practice recommendations; ORR will request a response and specify timeframes and disciplinary consequences for non-response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of secure facilities and transfer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: At secure facilities ORR reviews individual case files to ensure children placed in secure facilities are assessed at least every 30 days for the possibility of transfer to a less restrictive setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of long-term and transitional home care
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term home care and transitional home care facilities are subject to the same types of monitoring tailored to foster care arrangements; facilities providing services through sub-contracts/sub-grants must conduct annual monitoring/site visits of sub-recipients and weekly desk monitoring and provide findings to ORR on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider facility quality assurance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must develop quality assurance assessment procedures that accurately measure and evaluate service delivery in compliance with the regulations and 45 CFR part 411.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall report any emergency incident, significant incident, or program-level event and must document incidents with sufficient detail, in a trauma-informed manner and grounded in child welfare best practices, and update reports with findings made after the fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must never fabricate, exaggerate, or minimize incidents; must not use disparaging or judgmental language; must not use incident reporting or its threat to manage behavior; may not use reports of significant incidents as punishment or threat; a report's mere existence may not be the sole basis for step-up to restrictive placement or refusal to step down or refuse placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and ownership of case files
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities and PRS providers must preserve confidentiality of child case file records, protect from unauthorized use, and recognize records as the property of ORR; may not release records without ORR approval except limited program administration purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities and PRS providers must provide records to ORR immediately upon request; employees/former employees/contractors must not disclose case file records or information except for program administration and only after providing advanced notice to ORR so ORR can ensure disclosure compatibility with program goals and child safety/privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records maintenance and reporting to permit ORR oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain adequate records in the case file and make regular reports as required by ORR to permit monitoring and enforcement of these regulations and other ORR-determined requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior management: trauma-informed and evidence-based strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must develop behavior management strategies that include evidence-based, trauma-informed, and linguistically responsive program rules and policies that consider range of ages, maturity, and cultural sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies must not use negative reinforcement or consequences that are not constructive or not logically related to the behavior being regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited punitive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must not use or threaten corporal punishment, use significant incident reports as punishment, impose unfavorable consequences related to family/sponsor/unification or legal matters, force chores/work intended to demean, force physical movement (push-ups, running), place children in uncomfortable physical positions as punishment, search personal belongings solely for behavior management, or apply medical interventions not prescribed by a medical provider acting within professional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions extend to anything that increases risk of harm to the child or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sanctions that harm wellbeing or essential needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must not use sanctions that adversely affect a child's health or physical, emotional, or psychological well-being, or that deny meals, hydration, sufficient sleep, routine personal grooming, exercise (including daily outdoor activity), medical care, correspondence or communication privileges, or legal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of certain restraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must not use prone physical restraints, chemical restraints, or peer restraints for any reason in any care provider facility setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law enforcement involvement as last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: Involving law enforcement should be a last resort; calls to law enforcement may trigger evaluation of staff qualifications and training in trauma-informed de-escalation techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seclusion and restraint rules by facility type
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and RTCs are prohibited from using seclusion as behavioral intervention and are prohibited from using restraints except as described (personal restraint only in emergency safety situations). Secure facilities (except RTCs) may use personal restraints, mechanical restraints and/or seclusion in emergency safety situations and may restrain during transport/court/asylum interviews under specified individualized determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraints/seclusion must be used only to ensure safety and facilities must still provide mandated services to the greatest extent practicable while ensuring safety of the child and others; existence of individualized determinations required for some court/interview restraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft restraints limited use during transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities may only use soft restraints (e.g., zip ties and leg or ankle weights) during transport to and from secure facilities, and only when the care provider believes a child poses a serious risk of physical harm to self or others or a serious risk of running away from ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff training, vetting, and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs, restrictive placements, and PRS providers shall provide training to all staff, contractors, and volunteers to ensure understanding of ORR obligations and responsiveness to challenges faced by staff and children; trainings should be tailored to unique needs, attributes, and gender of children in care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard programs and restrictive placements must document completion of trainings in personnel files; all staff, contractors, and volunteers must complete required background checks and vetting prior to service provision and facilities must provide documentation of compliance to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff-to-child ratios and on-site case managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and restrictive placements shall meet staff-to-child ratios established by their States/licensing entities or by ORR if State licensure unavailable; must have case managers based on site at the facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access general obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the greatest extent practicable, programs shall consistently offer children the option of interpretation and translation services in their native or preferred language in a way they effectively understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to obtain a qualified interpreter, consult qualified ORR staff for guidance to ensure meaningful access; prioritize in-person qualified interpreters, especially for rare or indigenous languages, before professional telephonic services; translate all documents/materials shared with children in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement decisions consider language access
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall make placement decisions informed in part by language access considerations and other factors; ORR shall place children with similar language needs within the same program or restrictive placement to the extent appropriate and practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intake/orientation/confidentiality in preferred language
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to assessment and counseling, programs shall provide written notice of limits of confidentiality and orally explain the contents in the child's native or preferred language; conduct assessments and initial medical exams in that language; provide standardized comprehensive orientation in a language the child effectively understands regardless of reading level or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For step-ups/step-downs explain reasons in child's language; translate all documents into child's/sponsor's native/preferred language; if not literate or translations unavailable, have qualified interpreter orally or sign-language translate and explain and confirm comprehension; document acknowledgement of understanding in case files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education language access and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs shall provide educational instruction and materials in formats and languages accessible to all children, including in-person qualified interpreters, written translations, and telephonic interpretation when in-person options exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide recreational reading materials in accessible languages/formats; translate ORR-required documents used in lessons or orally translate/sign-language translate if written translations not available, prioritizing in-person interpreters first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious/cultural request accommodations in preferred language
rubrics_metrics.description: If a child requests religious and/or cultural information or items, the facility shall provide the requested items in the child's native or preferred language and as long as the request is reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent and sponsor communications language access
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs shall utilize necessary professional interpretation or translation to ensure meaningful access by a child's parent(s), guardian(s), and/or potential sponsor(s), and translate materials shared with them into their native or preferred language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthcare language access for medical encounters
rubrics_metrics.description: While providing or arranging healthcare services, programs shall ensure children can communicate with physicians, clinicians, and healthcare staff in their native or preferred language in a way they effectively understand, prioritizing in-person qualified interpreters before telephonic services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal services interpretation and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs shall make qualified interpretation/translation services available to children, child advocates, and legal service providers upon request while children are being provided with those services; such services shall be available in enclosed, confidential areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter/translator confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreters and translators shall keep all information about children's cases and/or services confidential from non-ORR grantees, contractors, and Federal staff and shall not disclose case file information to other interested parties in the child's cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR healthcare service obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall ensure all children in ORR custody are provided routine medical and dental care; access to medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement; family planning services; and emergency healthcare services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider healthcare responsibilities and network
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and restrictive placements must establish a network of licensed healthcare providers (specialists, emergency care, mental health, dental) that accept ORR's fee-for-service billing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial medical and dental exam timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete medical examination (including infectious disease screening) within 2 business days of admission (excluding weekends/holidays), unless recently examined; if children remain in ORR custody 60 to 90 days after admission, provide an initial dental exam or sooner if state licensing requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunization and annual exam requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate immunizations as recommended by the ACIP Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule and approved by CDC; provide an annual physical including hearing and vision screening and follow-up care for acute and chronic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medication administration, special diets, and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of prescribed medication and special diets; policies for safe, discreet, confidential provision of prescription and nonprescription medications, secure storage, controlled administration and disposal; licensed healthcare provider must write or orally order nonprescription medications and oral orders must be documented in the child's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental health interventions and communicable disease policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate mental health interventions when necessary and have policies and procedures for identifying, reporting, and controlling communicable diseases consistent with applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies enabling access to healthcare requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Have policies and procedures that enable children, including those with language/literacy barriers, to convey written and oral requests for emergency and non-emergency healthcare services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical isolation limited-use requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child may be placed in medical isolation to prevent spread of infectious disease or protect others, but isolation must be limited only to the extent necessary to ensure health and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medically isolated children must still be provided mandated services to the greatest extent practicable, be supervised under applicable ratios, and if multiple children are isolated they should be placed together when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and transfer for medically necessary care
rubrics_metrics.description: When a child's need for specialized services or medically necessary care is identified, ORR shall identify appropriate bed space and place the child at a facility able to provide or arrange such care and afford access to appropriate medical providers; if not immediately available ORR shall transfer the child as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation for medical care across state lines
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall ensure children have access to medical care, including transportation across State lines and ancillary services if necessary to access appropriate medical services, including specialists and family planning services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies regardless of whether Federal appropriations law prevents ORR from paying for the medical care itself; ORR will review conflicts with State law to ensure statutory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement for heightened medical needs or pregnancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall notify ORR within 24 hours of a child's need or request for medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement or the discovery of a pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of child advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates are third parties who make independent recommendations regarding the best interests of an unaccompanied child based on information obtained from the child and other sources (parents, family, potential sponsors, agencies, legal service providers, care provider representatives, health professionals, etc.).
